title: Motorway Signals & the Red X
whatItIs: Signals above the lanes and at the roadside warn of danger ahead. A red X closes a lane, and it is the law.

keyFacts.text: A red X above a lane means it is closed: you MUST NOT drive in that lane beyond the signal.
A speed limit shown in a red ring above your lane is the legal limit.
Red flashing lights and all lanes shown closed: the road is closed. You MUST NOT go beyond the sign in any lane.

keyFacts: Flashing amber lights warn of a hazard ahead: reduce your speed and be prepared for the hazard.

keyFacts.text: You MUST follow signs ahead of a closed lane and move safely to an open lane.

items.title: Red X over your lane
items.text: The lane is closed. Move to an open lane in good time.

items.title: Speed in a red ring
items.text: The legal limit for that stretch, even if the road looks clear.

items.title: All lanes shown closed
items.text: Red flashing lights with every lane shown closed: the road is closed. Don't go beyond the sign.

items.title: Flashing amber
items.text: Hazard ahead. Reduce your speed and be prepared for the hazard.

b.label: All lanes shown closed
points: Don't go beyond the sign in any lane

onTheTest.question: A red X is shown above your lane on a motorway. What does it mean?
options: The lane is closed: move to another lane
The lane is for breakdown vehicles
onTheTest.why: A red X closes the lane. You must not drive in that lane past the signal, usually because of an incident or people ahead.

traps: A red X is not advice: driving under it is an offence.
A speed in a red ring over the lanes is the legal limit, not a suggestion.
A roadside red X sign closes the lane it relates to. All lanes shown closed means the road is closed.
